name: Trigger
description: Pseudo-start node: the entry point of an orchestration, publishing the trigger payload (manual input, chatbot message, schedule tick, inbound email, or HTTP/API call) into the execution context.
handlerNote: Not a separate file in lib/orchestrations/nodes/. Handled inline in engine.ts's executeNodeByType() 'trigger' case; findTriggerNode()/getTriggerType() locate it and read its config.

inputSchema.description: Discriminant literal.
Which trigger mechanism starts this orchestration; drives node-compatibility checks (node-compatibility.ts) for the rest of the graph.
Only meaningful when triggerType is "schedule".

validationRules: None enforced in the node itself; engine.ts's isNodeCompatibleWithTrigger() uses triggerType to reject incompatible downstream nodes (data_capture, human_approval, workflow, file_parser) when triggerType is schedule/email/http_api.

outputShape.success: Always success:true (engine builds output directly from execution.triggerData, no failure path). Output is: { ...triggerData (spread to root), matchedPhrase, matchedIntent, trigger: { input: triggerData, timestamp, startedBy, startedAt, matchedPhrase, matchedIntent }, _system: { triggeredBy, executionId } }

preconditionsAndSideEffects: No external calls, DB writes, or LLM calls in the node itself.
Reads execution.triggerData / execution.triggeredBy / execution.startedAt already loaded by the caller.
permissionGating: None at node level. Access control for who/what can invoke the orchestration lives entirely at the trigger-definition level: ChatbotTriggerConfig.allowedRoles / allowedUsers (shared/orchestrationTypes.ts), enforced in lib/orchestrations/chatbot-trigger-matcher.ts, not in this pseudo-node's execution path.
riskTierRationale: Structural pseudo-node; no side effects of its own.

name: Workflow
description: Executes an existing Scout guided (browser-recorded) workflow, either via automated Puppeteer browser replay against a target URL or via the standard guided-workflow executor, optionally waiting for completion.

inputSchema.description: Discriminant literal.
TS-optional, but handler throws if absent/blank — effectively required at runtime. Must be a UUID.
Not referenced anywhere in the handler; appears unused.
Expression-evaluated. Passed through to executeGuidedWorkflow as informational context (falls back to the workflow's targetAppName if unset) — does not change execution mode.
Polls until the workflow finishes.
Maps workflow input keys to variable expressions evaluated against context.

Declared in the config type and accepted as a second parameter by the local mapWorkflowOutput() helper (which expects a Record<string,string>, not this array shape), but every call site in this handler invokes mapWorkflowOutput() with only one argument — config.outputMapping is never actually passed through, so this field is currently inert (see surprising findings).
If true, failures are swallowed into a {error, failed:true} output instead of failing the node.
Milliseconds; default 300000 (5 min) when waiting for completion.
If set, node is skipped (not failed) unless context.matchedPhrase/matchedIntent matches one of these.
Not read by this handler file.
Not read by this handler file.

validationRules: If triggerPhrases configured and context.matchedPhrase/matchedIntent don't match, returns { success:true, skipped:true } (soft skip, not an error).
workflowId required — throws "Workflow ID is required" if blank.
workflowId must match UUID regex /^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$/i, else throws with a diagnostic dump of available context keys.

outputShape.success: mapWorkflowOutput(...) => { executionId, workflowId, workflowTitle, status, steps, duration, ...executionResult.output }.
outputShape.failure: If continueOnFailure and waiting for completion: { ...output, error/timeout:true, failed:true }. Otherwise { success:false, error }.

preconditionsAndSideEffects: Calls executeGuidedWorkflow / waitForWorkflowCompletion (lib/guided-workflows/executor), which records server-side execution state — the actual step-by-step run happens client-side via the interactive Scout Player (public/scout-orchestration-player.js), which reports back through the /continue API route.
No LLM calls in this handler.

A previous "browser-automation mode" (targetUrl launching a real Puppeteer browser server-side) existed early on but was never used in practice and has been removed; targetUrl is now purely informational.
permissionGating: No role/permission check gates whether this node is allowed to run.
riskTierRationale: Triggers execution of a guided workflow (which can perform real actions via the client player), but no longer drives a privileged, unattended server-side browser session.

name: Data Capture
description: Injects a visual review/capture overlay into a live Puppeteer browser page (carried over from a prior Workflow node) so the frontend player can capture and let the user confirm data from the page.

inputSchema.description: Discriminant literal.
Capture strategy; not actually branched on in this handler (see surprising findings) — actual capture logic lives in the frontend player.
Default true; if not explicitly false, injects the overlay.
Default true (used by showReviewScreen(), which this handler never calls).
Seconds; 0 = require manual click (used by unused helper functions).
Milliseconds to wait before injecting the overlay, for dynamic content to settle.
Default "capturedData".
Declared in the type but not read anywhere in this handler.

validationRules: Requires context._browserPage (a Puppeteer Page) from a previous node (typically Workflow with 'close browser after workflow' unchecked); throws a descriptive error if absent.

outputShape.success: { [outputVariable]: {} (always an empty object — real capture happens client-side in the frontend player, not in this handler), _browserPage: page }

preconditionsAndSideEffects: Manipulates a live Puppeteer browser page: injects DOM overlay HTML/CSS/JS via page.evaluate().
No DB writes, no HTTP calls, no LLM calls in this handler.
Keeps the browser page open and passes it forward via _browserPage.
riskTierRationale: Manipulates a live browser page and can surface captured page data, but has no external network/DB writes of its own.

name: AI Extraction
description: Uses the configured LLM provider to extract structured data (predefined schema, a runtime chat instruction, or both) from an input value/template, optionally pausing to ask the chat user for missing mandatory fields.

inputSchema.description: Discriminant literal.
Default "predefined" in handler.
Declared in the type but not branched on in this handler.
Interpolated template; preferred source of input text.
Legacy single variable path, used only if `input` is blank.
Extra instructions appended to the user prompt; defaults to a generic extraction instruction.
Minutes before a pending clarification expires; default 15, floored at 1.
Preferred source of mandatory-field checks when present.
Field descriptors for predefined/hybrid extraction; also source of mandatory fields when `fields` is absent.
Where extracted data is stored; defaults to "extracted" if falsy at runtime.

validationRules: Input must resolve to a non-null, non-empty value (from `input` expression or `inputSource` path), else throws with a usage hint.
In "instruction" or "hybrid" mode, a non-empty runtime instruction (from trigger.input.userMessage / userMessage / trigger.matchedPhrase / matchedPhrase) is required, else throws.
LLM response must parse as JSON (optionally unwrapped from a ```json fence), else throws.
If config.schema has entries with required:true, validateAgainstSchema() throws if that key is entirely absent from the parsed result (only checks key presence, not value non-emptiness).

Separately, mandatory fields (from `fields` if provided, else required schema entries) are checked for a *meaningful* value (non-null/non-empty/non-empty-array/non-empty-object). If any are missing: on a chatbot-trigger context, the node pauses and asks a clarification question instead of failing; on any other trigger type, it throws ("Non-chat triggers must provide all mandatory inputs before continuing").

outputShape.paused: { success:true, paused:true, outputHandle:"clarification", output:{ [outputVariable]: partialExtractedData }, clarification:{ missingFields, message, questions, timeoutMinutes, expiresAt, fieldDefinitions } }

preconditionsAndSideEffects: Calls getLLMProvider() then provider.generate_answer(systemPrompt, userPrompt, inputText) — one LLM call per execution.
No DB writes and no direct HTTP calls in this handler (clarification persistence, if triggered, is written by engine.ts, not here).
riskTierRationale: LLM call only; no external side effects beyond the model call itself.

name: AI Task
description: Runs an arbitrary LLM generation/transformation task (summarize, draft, rewrite, etc.) using a configured instruction, a live chat message, or both, against optional context content resolved from earlier nodes, returning text or structured JSON.

inputSchema.description: Discriminant literal.
Determines where the task instruction comes from.
Required for static/hybrid modes; optional persona/guardrail text even in chat mode.
Interpolated template for context content, e.g. "{{parsedFile}}".
Controls prompt shape and response parsing.
Required (non-empty) when outputFormat is "json".
Defaults to "aiTask" if falsy at runtime.
Declared in the type; not actually read by this handler — chat-mode clarification uses a hardcoded 15-minute expiry instead.

validationRules: static mode: config.instruction required, else throws.
hybrid mode: combined (configInstruction + runtime chat message) must be non-empty, else throws "requires a base instruction in hybrid mode".

chat mode: resolves a runtime instruction from trigger.input.userMessage/userMessage/trigger.matchedPhrase/matchedPhrase, or (after a clarification resume) from `${outputVariable}.instruction`. If still empty: throws on non-chatbot triggers, or pauses with a clarification question ("What would you like me to do?") on chatbot triggers.
outputFormat "json" requires at least one entry in outputFields, else throws.
LLM JSON response must parse as an object, else throws "could not produce valid structured output".

outputShape.success: { [outputVariable]: string (text mode, code-fence-stripped) | object (json mode), [outputVariable+"Meta"]: { provider, model, instructionMode, instruction } }
outputShape.paused: { success:false, paused:true, clarification:{ message, expiresAt, fieldDefinitions } } (note: success is false here, unlike ai_extraction's paused success:true)

preconditionsAndSideEffects: Resolves companyId (via a DB lookup on company_target_applications from targetAppId when present, else a direct companyId in context) to select a possibly company-scoped LLM provider.
Calls getLLMProvider(companyId) then provider.generate_answer(...) — one LLM call per execution.
No other DB writes or HTTP calls in this handler.
riskTierRationale: LLM call only; no external side effects beyond the model call itself.

name: Knowledge Search
description: Runs a retrieval-only query against the company/target-app's RAG knowledge base (RetrievalEngine) and returns ranked passages plus citations; does not perform LLM synthesis itself (that's AI Task's job downstream).

inputSchema.description: Discriminant literal.
Interpolated template, e.g. "{{trigger.input.userMessage}}".
Default 5; clamped to [1, 20].
Defaults to "knowledgeSearch" if falsy at runtime.

validationRules: query must evaluate to a non-empty string, else throws.

companyId must be resolvable — preferentially derived from targetAppId via a DB lookup (a chatbot is always scoped to one target app, never company-level), falling back to a direct companyId in context; throws if neither resolves.
userId must resolve from _system.triggeredBy or trigger.startedBy, else throws.

outputShape.success: { [outputVariable]: formatted text of chunks ("Source: name (p.N)\ncontent" joined by "---"), [outputVariable+"Chunks"]: raw chunk array, [outputVariable+"Citations"]: citations array, [outputVariable+"Meta"]: { query, resultCount } }

preconditionsAndSideEffects: DB query on company_target_applications to derive companyId from targetAppId.
Calls RetrievalEngine.retrieve(companyId, userId, query, topK, targetAppId) — reads the vector/knowledge-base store; no LLM generation call in this handler.
permissionGating: None at node level; retrieval is scoped by companyId/targetAppId (tenant isolation), not by user role.
riskTierRationale: Read-only retrieval against the knowledge base.

name: Condition
description: Evaluates one or more variable comparisons (with and/or chaining) and routes execution down the "true" or "false" output handle; performs no context mutation.

inputSchema.description: Discriminant literal.

inputSchema.type: Array<{ variable, operator, value?, logicAfter?, caseSensitive? }>
inputSchema.description: operator is one of ConditionOperator (equals, not_equals, contains, not_contains, contains_any, contains_all, not_contains_any, greater_than, less_than, exists, not_exists, empty, not_empty). logicAfter ("and"|"or", default "and") applies between this condition and the next. caseSensitive defaults to false.

validationRules: conditions must be a non-empty array, else returns { success:false, error:"No conditions defined" } (not a thrown exception).
Conditions are evaluated left-to-right, combined pairwise via each condition's own logicAfter (no operator precedence/grouping).

outputShape.success: { success:true, outputHandle: "true" | "false" } — no `output` object is returned; context is never mutated by this node.

preconditionsAndSideEffects: None — pure in-memory evaluation via evaluateCondition() against the existing context. No DB, HTTP, or LLM calls.
riskTierRationale: Pure in-memory branching logic; no side effects.

name: Human Approval
description: Pauses the orchestration and requests a human approve/reject decision, creating an approval record and emailing the approver a review link.

inputSchema.description: Discriminant literal.
Can be a variable expression; evaluated at runtime.
Also used as the node execution's label and the email subject.

inputSchema.type: Array<{ name, label, type: "text"|"number"|"boolean"|"select", options?, editable, defaultValue? }>
inputSchema.description: Rendered into the approval request and the notification email body.
Minutes. Declared in the type but not read/enforced anywhere in this handler (no timeout/escalation logic present in the file).
Declared in the type but not used anywhere in this handler.

validationRules: approverEmail must evaluate to a non-empty string, else throws "Invalid approver email".
approverEmail must match /^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/, else throws "Invalid email format: ...".

outputShape.success (initial run, always pauses): { success:true, paused:true, output:{ approvalId, approvalPending:true, approver, approvalUrl } }
outputShape.resume (resumeAfterApproval, called sepa: { success:true, outputHandle: "approved"|"rejected", output:{ ...approvalResponse, approved, approvedAt, approvedBy, notes } }

preconditionsAndSideEffects: Writes a node-execution record via createNodeExecution (orchestration_node_executions).
Writes an approval record via createApproval (orchestration approvals table).

Sends an email to approverEmail via sendEmail() (lib/admin/email) containing the approval URL; if the email send fails, the error is logged but swallowed — the approval record still exists and the node still reports success/paused.
Generates a control-panel approval URL using NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL (or localhost:3000 fallback).
permissionGating: None at the node level — approverEmail is whatever the workflow author (or an upstream variable) configures; there is no role check restricting who may be named approver or who may act on the resulting approval URL within this handler.
riskTierRationale: Sends a real email and creates a durable, actionable approval URL, but exists specifically as a safety gate on further action.

name: Notification
description: Sends a notification through one or more channels (email, internal in-app, Microsoft Teams, Slack, SMS, WhatsApp) with per-channel retry and optional scheduled delivery; supports legacy single-channel config as well as the newer multi-channel `channels` config.

inputSchema.description: Discriminant literal.
Backward-compat path; normalizeChannels() maps these onto the multi-channel shape when `channels` is absent.

inputSchema.type: { enabled, senderCredentialId?, senderCredentialIdByEnvironment?{[environmentId]: credentialId}, fromName?, to?, cc?, bcc?, subject?, body?, bodyFormat?, attachments?[{name?,url?,contentType?}], priority?, delivery?{mode,scheduledAt}, retry?{enabled,maxAttempts,delaySeconds} }
inputSchema.description: senderCredentialId is the default sender; senderCredentialIdByEnvironment optionally overrides it per environment (set via the panel's per-environment picker, not by the planner) so a build can be promoted across environments without republishing.

inputSchema.type: { enabled, users?, roles?, teams?, groups?, title?, message?, notificationType?, actionLabel?, actionUrl?, expiryDate?, persistentUntilRead?, delivery?, retry? }
inputSchema.description: users/roles/teams/groups are CSV strings of ids or names used to target recipients.

inputSchema.type: { enabled, mentions?, title?, message?, messageFormat?, actionButtons?[{label,url}], webhookUrl?, delivery?, retry? }
{ enabled, mentions?, message?, messageFormat?, actionButtons?[{label,url}], threadTs?, webhookUrl?, delivery?, retry? }
{ enabled, senderId?, recipients?, message?, template?, unicodeSupport?, webhookUrl?, delivery?, retry? }

{ enabled, businessAccount?, senderNumber?, recipients?, messageType?, templateName?, templateLanguage?, templateVariables?, body?, mediaAttachment?, interactiveButtons?[{label,actionType,value}], webhookUrl?, delivery?, retry? }

validationRules: At least one channel must resolve to enabled:true, else throws "At least one notification channel must be enabled".

email: `to` and `body` required (after interpolation); a sender must resolve — the environment-specific override in `senderCredentialIdByEnvironment` if the execution's environment matches an entry, else the default `senderCredentialId` (throws "Email sender provider is required" if neither resolves).

internal: `message` required; at least one of users/roles/teams/groups required; resolving those to at least one active user id is required (throws "Unable to resolve any active internal recipients" otherwise).
teams: webhookUrl must be a valid http(s) URL; `message` required.
slack: webhookUrl must be a valid http(s) URL; `message` required.
sms: at least one recipient required; `message` required; webhookUrl (channel-level or NOTIFICATION_SMS_WEBHOOK_URL env var) must be a valid http(s) URL.

whatsapp: at least one recipient required; approved_template messages require templateName; session_message messages require body; webhookUrl (channel-level or NOTIFICATION_WHATSAPP_WEBHOOK_URL env var) must be a valid http(s) URL.
delivery.mode === "scheduled": scheduledAt must parse to a valid date, else throws; if that date is already in the past it's treated as immediate instead of scheduled.

retry.maxAttempts clamped to [1,10] (default 2), retry.delaySeconds clamped to [0,300] (default varies by channel, 1-2s), with exponential-ish backoff (delaySeconds fixed per attempt, not exponential) between attempts.

outputShape.success: { notificationSent:true, startedAt, completedAt, attemptedChannelCount, sentChannelCount, scheduledChannelCount, failedChannelCount, enabledChannels, channelResults:[{channel,status:"sent"|"scheduled"|"failed",attempts,sentAt?,scheduledFor?,error?,details?}] }
outputShape.failure: { success:false, error: 'Notification delivery failed for N channel(s): ...', output: <same shape as success, with notificationSent:false and per-channel failure details in channelResults> } — note failure still returns a populated output object.

preconditionsAndSideEffects: email channel: calls sendEmail() (lib/admin/email), resolving companyId/targetAppId from context for the send.

internal channel: resolves recipients via multiple DB reads — `users` table by id/email, `user_company_roles` joined to `roles` by role id/name, and optional `teams`/`team_members` or `user_teams`, and `groups`/`group_members` or `user_groups` tables (existence-checked via to_regclass before querying) — then INSERTs one row per recipient into `internal_notifications`.
teams/slack channels: outbound HTTP POST to the configured webhook URL (Adaptive Card / MessageCard for Teams; plain text or Block Kit for Slack).
sms/whatsapp channels: outbound HTTP POST to a configured or env-var-fallback webhook URL.
All channels retry per their retry config with a delay between attempts (setTimeout-based wait, not true exponential backoff here — contrast with api-call-node's backoff()).
permissionGating: None gates whether the node executes. The internal channel's users/roles/teams/groups fields are per-recipient TARGETING (who receives the notification, resolved against active users only via `status='active' AND deleted_at IS NULL`), not an execution permission check on the node itself.
riskTierRationale: Sends real outbound messages across email/Slack/Teams/SMS/WhatsApp/webhooks — genuine external communication that generally can't be undone once sent.

name: Variable
description: Sets one or more named context variables to either a literal value or an evaluated expression (supports {{...}} interpolation and basic math operators).

inputSchema.description: Discriminant literal.
value can be a literal or an expression like "{{capturedData.xxx}}".

validationRules: variables must be a non-empty array, else throws "At least one variable is required".
Each variable requires a non-empty `name`, else throws.
Each variable's `value` must not be undefined or "", else throws "Value is required for variable: <name>".
A value is treated as an expression (evaluated via evaluateExpression) if it contains "{{" or any of + - * / ( ) ; otherwise it is stored as a literal string.

outputShape.success: { [variable.name]: evaluatedValue | literalValue, ... } for every configured variable (via setVariablePath, so dotted names create nested paths).

preconditionsAndSideEffects: None — pure in-memory context mutation. No DB, HTTP, or LLM calls.

name: Data Formatter
description: Formats a value from context into a human-presentable string (pretty JSON, HTML table, plain-text table, CSV, key/value list, or a custom template) and stores it in a new output variable.

inputSchema.description: Discriminant literal.
Dotted path resolved against context.
Defaults to "pretty_json" if falsy at runtime.
Explicit column order/selection for table/csv formats; auto-inferred from the first 25 rows when omitted.
Supports {{json}}, {{value}}, {{rowCount}} placeholders; defaults to "{{json}}".
Default "No data available."
Default "" (empty string).
Default 100; clamped to [1, 1000].

validationRules: inputVariablePath required, else throws.
outputVariable required, else throws.

outputShape.success: { [outputVariable]: formattedString, [outputVariable+"Meta"]: { format, inputVariablePath, rowCount, columns, truncated (true if the source array exceeded maxRows) } }

preconditionsAndSideEffects: None — pure in-memory transform. No DB, HTTP, or LLM calls.

name: API Call
description: Makes an outbound HTTP(S) request (including optional mTLS) to a configured URL with flexible auth, body formats, path/query parameterization, and response field mapping, with retry/backoff and a configurable failure strategy.

inputSchema.description: Discriminant literal.
Expression-evaluated; e.g. "{{workflowId}}".
Defaults to "POST" if falsy.
Substitutes {name} and :name tokens in the URL.
enabled:false entries are skipped.
Both shapes are accepted.
Supports legacy flat fields and structured sub-objects (apiKey/bearerToken/basic/oauth2/customHeaders/mtls).
Defaults to "none" for GET/HEAD/OPTIONS, else "json".
Used for json/raw_text/xml/binary bodies; JSON mode supports {{expr}} interpolation with correct in-string JSON escaping.
isFile:true fields are read from local disk via readFile().
Base64 payload for bodyFormat "binary" (falls back to requestBodyTemplate).
Additional multipart file fields, read from local disk.
JSONPath-ish (dot/bracket) mapping merged with responseFieldMappings.
Sanitized to [a-zA-Z0-9_]; default "apiResult".
Comma list of exact codes, "NNN-NNN" ranges, or "Nxx" wildcards; default 2xx.
Default true (raw body included unless explicitly false).
Milliseconds; clamped to [100, 300000].
Clamped to [0, 10]; total attempts = retryAttempts + 1.
Base delay for exponential backoff between retries (delay * 2^(attempt-1)).
stop -> node fails; continue/alert -> node reports success with failure details in output (alert additionally console.warns).

validationRules: apiUrl required (post-interpolation), else throws.

auth type-specific: api_key needs both name and value; bearer needs a token; basic needs a username; oauth2 with tokenUrl needs clientId+clientSecret (and username+password for the "password" grant type); mTLS needs certPath and keyPath.
JSON request body must remain valid JSON after variable interpolation, else throws with parse error detail.
binary body requires binaryBodyBase64 or requestBodyTemplate, else throws.
form-data file fields require filePath, else throws.

Retries only for retryable failures: HTTP 408/429/5xx, or network/timeout errors (ENOTFOUND/ECONNREFUSED/ECONNRESET/EAI_AGAIN/timeout/AbortError); auth (401/403) and JSON-parse errors are treated as non-retryable.

outputShape.success: { requestMethod, requestUrl, httpStatusCode, responseHeaders, responseBody, parsedJson, rawResponse? (if includeRawResponse!==false), executionDurationMs, attempts, mappedFields, [outputVariableName]: {...all of the above, mappedFields} }
outputShape.failure (failureStrategy=continue|alert): { success:true, output:{ ...priorOutput, apiCallFailed:true, error, errorDetails, httpStatusCode, responseHeaders, responseBody, parsedJson, rawResponse, executionDurationMs, attempts } }

preconditionsAndSideEffects: Sends a real outbound HTTP request to apiUrl (via fetch, or Node's https.request for mTLS).
May perform a second outbound HTTP request to an OAuth2 token endpoint to obtain a bearer token.
May read local files from disk (readFile) for form-data file fields, additional fileUploads, and mTLS cert/key/ca material.
Retries with exponential backoff on retryable failures.
permissionGating: None. Auth headers containing secrets are masked in logs (shouldMask()/maskValue()) but this is log hygiene, not an access-control gate.
riskTierRationale: Arbitrary outbound HTTP(S) request, potentially with real credentials/mTLS, to any URL the config specifies.

name: Database
description: Uses the LLM to assess whether a natural-language database request is answerable against a configured, tenant-scoped schema and, if so, generate a single safe read-only SQL SELECT query — it generates and validates SQL but does not execute it against any database.

inputSchema.description: Discriminant literal.
TS-optional, but handler throws if blank — effectively required.
Default "databaseQuery".
Default "userMessage"; several context fallbacks are also tried (trigger.input.userMessage/message, message, query).
Default "extracted".
Optional extra context path.
Default 25; clamped to [1, 500]. Injected as a LIMIT if the generated SQL doesn't already have one.
Appended to both the readiness-assessment and SQL-generation prompts.
Default false — SELECT * is rejected unless explicitly allowed.
Default 15, floored at 1.

validationRules: schemaId required, else throws.
companyId must resolve (runtimeOptions.companyId or context companyId/trigger.input.companyId), else throws.
The resolved schema row must exist, be active, non-deleted, and belong to the resolved company/target app, else throws "Selected database schema is unavailable or inactive for this target app."
An LLM readiness assessment runs first; if not ready and confidence >= 0.65 with a question present: on a chatbot-trigger context the node pauses for clarification, otherwise it throws.

Generated SQL is validated by validateSafeSelectQuery(): non-empty; single statement only (rejects multiple `;`-separated statements); must start with SELECT; rejects a denylist of keywords/patterns (insert/update/delete/drop/alter/truncate/create/grant/revoke/merge/execute/call/copy/vacuum/analyze/comment, `--`, `/*`, `*/`, `union`, `into`); must contain a FROM clause; rejects `SELECT *` unless allowSelectStar is true.
If the LLM's SQL is empty/unparseable, a fallback query is heuristically built by scoring table/column name matches against extracted fields and the request text.
A LIMIT (or FETCH FIRST ... ROWS ONLY) clause is force-appended if not already present.

outputShape.paused: { success:true, paused:true, outputHandle:"clarification", output:{ [outputVariable]: {schemaName, databaseType, capturedInput, readiness, notExecuted:true} }, clarification:{ missingFields, message, questions, timeoutMinutes, expiresAt, fieldDefinitions } }
outputShape.failure: { success:false, error, output:{ databaseNodeError:{ message, notExecuted:true } } }

preconditionsAndSideEffects: DB read of target_app_database_schemas joined to company_target_applications, scoped by schemaId + companyId (+ optional targetAppId) and is_active/deleted_at filters — this is the only database access in the entire handler.
Two LLM calls per execution: one for the readiness assessment, one for SQL generation (via getLLMProvider(companyId).generate_answer).
Does NOT connect to or execute against the target application's actual database — the generated SQL is returned as data only (notExecuted:true is set on every output path).
permissionGating: None role-based. Tenant isolation is enforced by scoping the schema lookup query to the resolved companyId (and target app), not by a user permission check.
riskTierRationale: Never executes SQL itself (notExecuted:true always), but generates real SQL against tenant schema metadata that a downstream step (e.g. api_call) may go on to execute.

name: File Parser
description: Parses a chat-attached file (referenced by a dotted context path) into either plain text or, for CSV, structured row objects, pausing to ask the user to attach a file if one isn't present.

inputSchema.description: Discriminant literal.
Dotted path into context to an attachment reference { id, name, fileType, storagePath, sizeBytes }, e.g. "trigger.input.attachments.0".
structured is CSV-only.

validationRules: sourceVariablePath required, else throws.
outputVariable required, else throws.

The resolved value must look like an attachment reference (has storagePath and fileType); if not found at sourceVariablePath, it also checks `${outputVariable}.attachment` (the shape the engine writes after a clarification resume). If still absent, the node pauses asking the user to attach a file rather than failing.
A parser must exist for the attachment's fileType (getDocumentParser), else throws.
extractMode "structured" is only supported when fileType === "csv"; any other file type throws.

outputShape.success (structured mode): { [outputVariable]: Array<Record<string,string>> (parsed CSV rows), [outputVariable+"Meta"]: { fileName, fileType, rowCount } }

preconditionsAndSideEffects: Reads the file's bytes from blob/object storage via getStorageProvider().get_file(storagePath).

Parses the buffer via getDocumentParser(fileType).parse(buffer) (document-processing pipeline; may include OCR/PDF/DOCX parsing depending on registered parsers — not confirmed to call an LLM from this file).
Uses a hand-rolled RFC4180-aware CSV row parser included directly in this file (no external CSV dependency).
permissionGating: None at node level. Enforced elsewhere: node-compatibility.ts lists file_parser as an INTERACTIVE_NODE, so orchestration-level validation rejects it on automated triggers (schedule/email/http_api) since there's no live chat attachment to read in that context.
riskTierRationale: Read-only access to a chat-attached file already in the tenant's own storage.

name: For Each
description: Iterates an array from context, running one of a fixed allow-list of body node types (API Call, Notification, AI Extraction, Variable, Data Formatter) once per item, collecting per-iteration results.

inputSchema.description: Discriminant literal.
Dotted path to the array to iterate, e.g. "rows" (often a File Parser node's structured output).
Context key each element is bound to per iteration, e.g. "item"; defaults to "item" if blank.
User-configured soft cap; the executor hard-ceilings this regardless (see validation).
Defaults to true unless explicitly false; if false, iteration stops at the first failed item.
Only these five types are runnable inside a loop body — notably excludes the interactive-only nodes (data_capture, human_approval, workflow, file_parser).
Config for whichever bodyNodeType is selected.
Defaults to "loopResults" if blank.

validationRules: sourceVariablePath required, else throws.
outputVariable required, else throws.
bodyNodeType required, else throws.
The value at sourceVariablePath must be an array, else throws "No array found at ... For Each requires a list to iterate."

maxIterations is clamped to [1, 500] (HARD_ITERATION_CEILING) regardless of the configured value — an explicit hard cap independent of user config, because each iteration can fan out a real side effect (API call, notification, LLM call) per item.
If items.length exceeds the clamped max, the excess is silently truncated (truncated:true is reported in the meta output, not an error).

outputShape.success: { [outputVariable]: Array<{ index, item, success, output?, error? }> (one entry per processed item), [outputVariable+"Meta"]: { totalItems, processedItems, succeeded, failed, truncated } }
outputShape.failure: { success:false, error } — only if a top-level precondition fails (e.g. no array found); individual item failures do not fail the node unless continueOnItemFailure is false, in which case the loop stops early but still returns success:true with partial results.

preconditionsAndSideEffects: Delegates each iteration to the matching body-node executor (executeApiCallNode / executeNotificationNode / executeAIExtractionNode / executeVariableNode / executeDataFormatterNode), so it inherits whatever side effects that body type has (outbound HTTP calls, notification sends/DB writes, LLM calls) — repeated up to the clamped iteration count.
No side effects of its own beyond the delegated body node calls.
permissionGating: None at node level. node-compatibility.ts does not list for_each as an INTERACTIVE_NODE, so it's usable with automated triggers (schedule/email/http_api) as well as interactive ones — consistent with its bodyNodeType allow-list deliberately excluding the interactive-only node types.
riskTierRationale: Multiplies whatever side effects its body node type has (up to 500x) — inherits and amplifies the risk of api_call/notification, its two highest-risk allowed body types.

name: End
description: Pseudo-finish node: assembles the orchestration's final response (selected output variables, optional per-node response log, and an optional user-facing display message/table/JSON payload) and always completes the execution successfully.
handlerNote: Not a separate file in lib/orchestrations/nodes/. Handled inline in engine.ts's executeNodeByType() 'end' case via the private buildEndNodeOutput() method.

inputSchema.description: Discriminant literal.
Whether to render `message` as the chatbot's final answer; if false/absent, the final answer defaults to "Workflow completed successfully."
Template rendered with {{...}} interpolation against context when displayMessage is true.
Default "text"; drives the structured `display` payload for table/json modes.
Path resolved against context for table/json display data.
Optional ordered table columns; inferred when omitted (inference itself happens client-side — this node just passes the array through).
Variable paths resolved and collected into `selectedOutputs`.
Default "finalResponse"; where the assembled response object is stored.
If true, includes the full context._nodeResponses map (every node's output logged so far) in the final response.

validationRules: None — every field is optional and has a safe default; this node cannot fail.

outputShape.success: Always succeeds. Sets context[responseVariablePath] = { executionId, orchestrationId, completedAt, selectedOutputs, nodeResponses? }. Also sets context._chatbot = { ...existing, finalAnswer, finalResponsePath, display? } where display is a { type:"table", dataPath, data, columns } or { type:"json", dataPath, data } object when displayMode is table/json.

preconditionsAndSideEffects: None — pure in-memory context assembly. No DB, HTTP, or LLM calls.
Engine records this node's execution as "completed" and ends the run (end nodes have no outgoing connections to follow).
riskTierRationale: Pure in-memory finalization; cannot fail or produce side effects.
